title: A valuation ring is a normal domain
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring that is a valuation ring: $A$ is a domain with fraction field $K$, and for every $x\in K^\times$ either $x\in A$ or $x^{-1}\in A$. Then $A$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], i.e. every element of $K$ integral over $A$ belongs to $A$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00IC (lemma-valuation-ring-normal, line 11783), statement and proof

proof.text: Let $x\in K$ be integral over $A$. If $x=0$, then $x\in A$. Otherwise, choose a monic equation $x^n+a_{n-1}x^{n-1}+\cdots+a_0=0$ with $n\geq1$ and all $a_i\in A$. Such an equation exists by the definition of integral, and degree zero is impossible because $K$ is a field.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00IC (lemma-valuation-ring-normal), statement; elementary argument from the displayed valuation criterion

proof.text: The valuation-ring hypothesis gives $x\in A$ or $y=x^{-1}\in A$. In the first case there is nothing to prove. In the second, multiply the monic equation by $x^{-(n-1)}$ to obtain $x=-\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}a_i y^{n-1-i}\in A$, since every term on the right lies in $A$. This formula also covers $n=1$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00IC (lemma-valuation-ring-normal), conclusion; direct proof from the equivalent valuation criterion in the node statement

proof.text: Thus every element of the fraction field integral over $A$ lies in $A$. Together with the assumed domain property, this is exactly that $A$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring].
